findings.title: KeyError crash when existing Integration has no "sender" metadata
findings.body: In GitHubInstallation.dispatch, the new ownership check does `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]`. The "sender" key is only present for integrations created from the GitHub `installation` webhook; integrations created through the normal Sentry pipeline never get a "sender" key (build_integration only copies state["sender"], and nothing in the pipeline ever binds "sender"). If an ACTIVE integration without an OrganizationIntegration and without sender metadata is reached here — e.g., a pipeline-created integration whose Sentry organization was later deleted, or one left behind by a partially failed install — this line raises KeyError, returning a 500 instead of the intended github-integration-failed page and permanently blocking re-installation for that installation_id. Use `integration.metadata.get("sender")` and fail closed with the friendly error when it is absent.

findings.title: OAuth token exchange and user-info fetch can raise unhandled exceptions, producing a 500
findings.body: In OAuthLoginView.dispatch, `req = safe_urlopen(url=ghip.get_oauth_access_token_url(), data=data)` is outside the try/except that only wraps safe_urlread/parse_qsl. A connection error, timeout, or RestrictedIPAddress from sentry.http raises here, and there is no exception handler in the pipeline dispatch path, so a transient GitHub/network failure during installation surfaces as a 500 rather than the graceful error page this PR adds. The same applies to `get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` on line 434, which performs another network call that can raise. Both calls should be wrapped so failures render the github-integration-failed page as the PR intends.

findings.title: Ownership check compares mutable GitHub usernames instead of immutable user IDs
findings.body: The new check compares `pipeline.fetch_state("github_authenticated_user")` against `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]`, i.e. it compares GitHub login names. GitHub usernames are mutable and recyclable: (a) if the user who installed the app later renames their GitHub account, the stored sender login no longer matches and that legitimate user can never link or re-link the installation; (b) conversely, if an attacker registers the abandoned old username, they satisfy this check and can attach the victim's GitHub App installation (installation IDs are sequential and guessable) to their own Sentry organization. Both the webhook sender payload and the /user API response include the immutable numeric user `id`; the check should compare IDs instead of logins.

findings.title: test_installation_not_found no longer exercises the installation-404 path
findings.body: test_installation_not_found stubs a 404 for GET /app/installations/{installation_id}, but it submits state "ddd023d87a913d5226e2a882c4c4cc05", which does not match the pipeline signature used throughout these tests ("9cae5e88803f35ed7970fc131e6e65d3"). The request is therefore rejected at OAuthLoginView's state check and the flow never reaches build_integration, so the 404 stub is never called and the "The GitHub installation could not be found." branch in build_integration is left uncovered by any test (the assertion on "Invalid installation request." passes because of the signature mismatch, not the missing installation). Either drive the flow with the correct state and a bound installation_id so the 404 path is exercised, or rename the test to reflect that it now only tests signature validation.
